HRA Analysis: An even field kicks off the night, where LADY IN LINE (10) uses her mares claim to gain entry into the race and should be suited by what looks likely to be a solid tempo throughout. That is normally the case when the veteran KENYA (9) is involved. He has been a bit hit and miss of late but, at his best, should be in the finish and should also give those driven quietly off the speed their chance to run home strongly. OUR DANCE MONKEY (2) draws well and has been favoured in the market in her two starts in the state. She has been over-racing, but if she settles better in the run, you would expect her to be competitive in this class of field. SPORT WATCHER (1) should receive a nice soft pegs run and get her chance late if the gaps appear. REALLY SMARTIE (4) was well backed when saluting last start after getting off the pegs at the right time, but draws a somewhat awkward gate here. EYE SEE AMOUR (8), IAMAHUNTER (11) and OLLIES MEDAL (12) wouldn't surprise to see running home strongly off a slow tempo if they bring their best. Selections:LADY IN LINE (10), OUR DANCE MONKEY (2), KENYA (9), SPORT WATCHER (1)

The first Evicus heat for the two-year-old tasbred fillies looks the stronger of the two, where VINJETTA (3) will be looking to break through for a well-deserved victory after some very handy efforts in the Sweepstakes features in previous months. ELEANOR STREET (2) makes her way down after a handy second at Young first up and looks an improving type, who should get every chance from the nice draw. DANGER BEWARE (4) looks the best of the unraced trio off her trials, where she has run home strongly on both occasions. SHEEZSOTINY (1) has shown good gate speed in both starts and should be looking to hold a forward position, where she could be in the finish with natural improvement. SOUL OF KARALTA (6) may be the one that presses the button early from out wide and could be the one over the odds, having shown good ability when putting it all together in her three starts to date. Selections:VINJETTA (3), ELEANOR STREET (2), DANGER BEWARE (4), SOUL OF KARALTA (6)

BETTOR THAN READY (1) couldn't have been any more impressive in his four starts to date, including winning the Sweepstakes feature in August. Unsure if he will have enough gate speed to hold the front, but in a small field and with no bad luck, he should take plenty of holding out late. POGACAR (4) put together two really nice performances before resuming with a nice second from the back. Expect there will be some improvement off that run, and he looks the clear testing material for the expected favourite. OUR ROB ROY (3) hasn't been far away behind some handy ones of late, and expect it to be no different here. MYSTERY MAIL (6) was seen hitting the line very well last start and has shown some good glimpses of ability throughout his career to date, so could be the one at odds if things go his way. DARCY BE DREAMING (5) was disappointing first up from a break after doing the work outside the leader, but may look to use his sharp gate speed to attempt to find the pegs here from the awkward draw, which would give him a chance to be in the finish. Selections:BETTOR THAN READY (1), POGACAR (4), MYSTERY MAIL (6), OUR ROB ROY (3)

TAPPY (2) looks the most progressive horse in this field. From the good draw, he should sit somewhere on speed with cover and get his chance to notch up another victory. PHLOW JO (1) rises slightly in class but looks to be finally putting it all together with a couple of wins of late. From the nice draw and with her sufficient gate speed, she should be able to look to hold the lead or at worst, get her chance up the sprint lane late. MY WAY (4) will most likely look to use his sharp gate speed in an attempt to find the pegs and continues to drop in grade, so he should get his chance in what looks a somewhat even field. TULLAH GIRL (3) is a consistent mare and only needs to bring her recent form into this race to be running home strongly. She may be hard to hold out if there is some genuine tempo throughout up front. CAN FEEL THE FURY (5) looks the best of the rest and has been going better than his figure form suggests at his past couple after some handy placings previously. Selections:TAPPY (2), PHLOW JO (1), MY WAY (4), TULLAH GIRL (3)

The well-bred RAZZAMATAZ (5) was backed and duly saluted first up, winning somewhat easily in the end. No doubt she will continue to improve with racing and should take plenty of holding out here. KOOKY (4) arrives back in the state after competing in the Nutrien Classic series at Wagga . Her two trials since have been handy enough to suggest she looks the logical danger, especially if she works forward to find the front, which I suspect BETTYS GIRL (2) may look to hand over this week after disappointing as a short-priced favourite when leading last start. MON BELLE AMOUR (1) gets the pole draw and comes off the back of a handy trial effort, looking the best of the two on debut. FARRAHS LEGACY (3) can do a few things wrong, as seen in some of her trial performances, but it wouldn't surprise to see her take this out if she puts her best foot forward. Selections:RAZZAMATAZ (5), KOOKY (4), BETTYS GIRL (2), MON BELLE AMOUR (1)

Would expect CALZO SNIPER (5) to zoom to the front and find the pegs here again, which will give him his best chance. Stepping out to the 2090-metre distance for the first time does bring some question marks for not only him but the rest of the field. His chances may also rely on how aggressively FARROH JOE (7) is driven throughout, who brings some handy Victorian form to the state and is normally driven on speed. LOTSEVEN (6) looks an improving type the more he races and looked sharp in a trial on Monday, making him one of the clear fancies. STABLE TALK (3) won nicely last week and I would expect him to look to cross those to his inside and get his chance up the sprint lane behind the expected leader. BUILTTHEMANASTATUE (4) is an interesting runner on the somewhat quick back-up after competing in South Australia last Wednesday. He has run some handy races in quality fields throughout his career to date, so can't be left out. Selections:LOTSEVEN (6), CALZO SNIPER (5), FARROH JOE (7), STABLE TALK (3)

The low-class race of the night should see at least a moderate tempo, with KIAVINO STRIDE (7) drawing the front row and no doubt looking to push forward from his gate. He once again looks one of the leading fancies, although he is yet to get the job done when looking likely in his past couple of starts in suitable races. COLORADO GIRL (6) could be the improver in the field and has been going better than her figure form suggests. She should be running home strongly if she brings her best form. STAROFREMEMBRANCE (5) and JAY MILLER (3) will be reliant on some tempo to allow them to run home strongly, as they usually do. BARBETTE (4) should push forward from her middle front-row draw to find a position on speed, while HALIS BOY (8) could be the one at odds as the lone back-row runner. Selections:JAY MILLER (3), KIAVINO STRIDE (7), COLORADO GIRL (6), BARBETTE (4),

The higher-class race of the night doesn't have a whole lot of strong figure form to digest. ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (8) is a consistent pacer who likes to race on speed and has been competitive in fields stronger than what he meets tonight. Expect him to be put into the race at some point and look to out-tough them. LYNRYD SKYNRYD (4) should be able to use his sharp gate speed to find the pegs and gets his chance to return to form, while KOSTYUK LEIS (6) should be suited by the smaller field and, if anywhere near her best, may take some holding out late. ALWAYS AURORA (1) put in a much-improved effort last start, making good ground from back in the field, and although steps up in class here, gets the pole draw to its advantage. MONTGOMERY BURNS (3) has been thereabouts in Tier 1 races of late and should find a nice spot on speed to get his chance, while IMPERIAL LAZ (7) could be the one at odds. Selections:ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (8), LYNRYD SKYNRYD (4), MONTGOMERY BURNS (3), ALWAYS AURORA (1)

The final race of the night is over the short distance, where KUHIO KREST (3) will be looking for back-to-back victories after proving too strong in a similar grade last start. There should be some okay tempo early, with NOELS GIFT (1) and FEELINGKINDALUCKY (4) looking to push forward from their draws, while PARK LANE (5) should zoom straight to the front with his exceptional gate speed. Although he has put in some improved performances of late, he would need to improve again here to be holding on in the finish. QUEENOFDANCE (7) has almost been dominating this grade of late and should be suited by the small field despite her awkward front-row draw. TWILIGHT BEACH (6) is another who would benefit from a solid tempo throughout and, at her best, would be hard to hold out late if she gets the right run in transit. Selections:KUHIO KREST (3), QUEENOFDANCE (7), TWILIGHT BEACH (6), PARK LANE (5) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

CASTERTON (6) was very impressive at Kilmore last start when he defeated HEAVENLY GEM by 4 metres. He looks extremely hard to beat tonight. His stable and driver must be respected. ONE AUSSIE (8), MAIN BEACH (7) and UP THE BOMBER (9) look like the other chances.

LAMBRO LOUELLA (1) was extremely impressive two starts back at Globe Derby when she ran second behind LEVIOSA and made a good amount of ground. She was a last start winner at Horsham last start as well. She will love the inside draw tonight. RANKINE (8) has won his first two starts. He was very impressive two starts back here at Globe Derby when he took out the Lordship. JADES REASON (3) and SOUTH AUSSIE STAR (4) are also chances.

SPRINGFIELD AFFAIR (3) has won four of his last five starts and looks like a different horse since racing in New South Wales. He is well drawn and looks extremely hard to beat tonight. THE LAST TRIP (5) looks like a big danger after winning five from his last six starts. He is a big threat tonight. FOLLOWTHEACE (2) and HOT DEAL (1) are also chances.

SOUTH SEAS ROCK (8) has a very awkward draw to overcome but his recent win in Menangle was very impressive when he ran a mile rate of 1.52.7. He is a big chance again tonight. FORTY LOVE (10) has been running out of his skin in Victoria. He was impressive last start at Horsham and he should be right in the finish tonight. ROCKIN GEMMA (6) and ATA RANGI (5) are also chances.

MY ULTIMATE BARNEY (8) is another who will need some luck from the draw but he has been in some strong feature races in Melbourne recently and if he is anywhere near his best tonight then he will be hard to beat. ULTIMATE VINNIE (6) is a big danger and has a strong record here at Globe Derby. ROADMASTER (7) and FLY THE BANNER (4) are also chances.

SANTA CASA LANE (5) ran a handy race behind DELIGHTFUL DREAM a fortnight ago here at Globe Derby. He has plenty of ability and looks like a big threat tonight. JACKIE DANIELS (4) won easily here at Globe Derby earlier in the week when she defeated KEAYANG SHADOWBOX by 9.7 metres. She is a big chance again tonight. ROAD STAR (1) and RESURRECTS (6) are also chances.

TUFFASNAILS (6) has won two of his last three starts. He defeated NORMY by 19.4 metres at Port Pirie last start. He has been a big improver recently and it’s hard to see him getting beaten tonight. TWIN CONNECTION (8) looks like a big danger even with the tricky draw after winning three of his last four starts. DIDMESELFAMISCHIEF (9) and STYLISTIK (10) are also chances.

LETSSTARTINHEAVEN (2) is another who has been extremely impressive in NSW and Queensland. He is well drawn tonight and he should be able to lead all of the way. ZANDA MAN (7) is a really classy operator who has won two of his last four starts. He is a big danger even with the tricky draw. DELIGHTFUL DREAM (6) and DON CRUNCH (1) look the next best.

MAJOR BLITZ (5) has won some really good races in some Melbourne Juvenile feature races. He is a big chance tonight in a race like this. LUVTOBEUPTOME (6), LOCHINVAR LEADER (4) and IM BIG BUSINESS (3) are also chances.

REOFFENDER (5) has won three of his last four starts. Tonight will be a lot tougher but I love the way he has been going about it. He is worth strong consideration. JOHNS BOY (6), THE VICARS GIRL (4) and SOLOTREKK (3) are also chances.

ARTIGAS (1) ran second at Melton last start. He has the recent form on his side but this is his first stand start which is the main concern. REGAL ATTIRE (8) looks like a big threat tonight and could easily return to the winners list. ALL THE TRIX (6) and MAESTRO (3) are also chances. OVERVIEW: Plenty of chances in this clash to start the night at Beckley Park, but ARZALI ROCKSTAR (7) looks ready to break through after back-to-back second placings in recent weeks. Two ago, she was trapped parked, did a power of work and was only nailed late, and then last Friday led before being out-sprinted by the handy Sandelton in a slick enough last half. The gate isn’t ideal, but she’s narrowly favoured. VIVA STORM (6) made the Group 2 final of the Vicbred Super Series for four-year-old mares before closing off nicely from last when sixth at Kilmore last week, YANKEE RAIN (10) has won her last two after recently joining the Tom Rundle barn and is an obvious threat, while Alex Hurley’s lovely grey SPUN SILVER (5) probably has the early toe to lead and should run well from there over the sprint trip. Hard race where plenty of others can win! SELECTIONS: ARZALI ROCKSTAR (7), VIVA STORM (6), YANKEE RAIN (10), SPUN SILVER (5)

OVERVIEW: MISS MUSCLE (9) is the two-year-old up against older horses, but she brings in some nice formlines for this 0/1-win event. Tom Rundle’s filly finished fourth despite a tough run in the Group 1 Vicbred Super Series final last month, before making a mistake in the Tatlow Stakes. She then ran a really good race from well back in transit for second to Night Flight at Ballarat. Good draw here and she looks the one to beat. Always had time for SHINELIKETHESUN (10), who did some very impressive things at stages last campaign but just struggled to put it all together. Freshened and back to the races, there’s a big watch on her. I think she’s above average. They look the main winning hopes, but respect is given to others such as THE PASO DOBLE (1), NO REPENTANCE (2), ALECTRONA (3) and DESERT ROYALE (6), who might have the speed to cross first-up from a break. SELECTIONS: MISS MUSCLE (9), SHINELIKETHESUN (10), ALECTRONA (3), THE PASO DOBLE (1)

OVERVIEW: Another wide-open race where a case can be made for plenty, including the consistent ALLWATFUNJINGLES (1). He’s certainly no superstar, but is very capable in this type of grade and importantly draws to settle closer to the speed than he has in recent starts. He’s been hitting the line nicely from well back in transit, including on October 2 at Melton when he was held up and flashed late to be narrowly beaten behind Met With A Shrug and CHINSKI (2). If he can settle behind the likely leader in CHINSKI (2), he should be able to give this a shake. CHINSKI (2) was caught parked last time at Kilmore and dropped out, but all his recent form is strong and he’s likely to run from the front, the first-up BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (5) hasn’t raced since March and heads to Geelong without a trial, but possesses a good finishing burst when her manners are in check, while LOVE WHO (4) was a good winner at Shepparton in mid-August, then ran well for second at Maryborough before a tough trip and down-the-track finish at Horsham last time out. BACK: ALLWATFUNJINGLES (1) – 1.5 units (each-way) SELECTIONS: ALLWATFUNJINGLES (1), CHINSKI (2), BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (5), LOVE WHO (4)

OVERVIEW: BANIA (2) steps out on debut here for David Barbetti and Mick Stanley, and I suspect he can make a winning start in this maiden event. He beat the handy Magellan in a trial at Maryborough back in July and then ran really well in a subsequent hit-out at Melton when closing off nicely from last to be beaten 5.6m in a 57.3 last half. He then won his most recent effort back at Maryborough on October 4. Happy his way. RIDE HIGH CAPTIN (8) brings clearly the best form into this maiden assignment, with runner-up placings from his last two outings. Two back, he led and was run down by the smart King Baldwin with a big margin back to third, and then wobbled around the corner at Ballarat, regained the lead and was nailed late by Ultimate Grange. He has won a Bacchus Marsh trial since and looks sure to go close in this. The others would surprise. BACK: BANIA (2) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: BANIA (2), RIDE HIGH CAPTIN (8), KATUNTI (7), SONOFPLATINUM (1)

OVERVIEW: He’s not the horse you’d bet your last dollar on, but COLTRANE (4) is one that might give you some thrills as he’s a quirky customer with loads of ability who will be very good when he puts everything together. He ruined his chances with a gallop when favourite in a 0W/15.0K stake race before a spell and has come back with two nice trials, including one where he was only 3.5m off unbeaten star two-year-old Verbici. He’s won four from 18 and there looks to be some serious scope there. EL TORNADO (5) took a while to warm up this campaign but has won his last two in really nice style at Melton and Ballarat, lightly-raced five-year-old LORD LOGAN (6) is back in Victoria after an early gallop at Globe Derby took him out of winning contention on October 3 and he’s capable of returning to winning form, while KYVALLEY JETSTREAM (7) hasn’t shown much in two runs back from a break but has ability and is dropping in grade. BACK: COLTRANE (4) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: COLTRANE (4), EL TORNADO (5), LORD LOGAN (6), KYVALLEY JETSTREAM (7)

OVERVIEW: SERIOUSLY SAL (2) ran second in the Vicbred Super Series two-year-old consolation two starts back at Ballarat and performed okay in a subsequent race at Melton last Friday despite being well beaten by a few rivals with good promise. This looks much easier, and from the good draw she must be rated a good chance. THE WOOL BROKER (4) started favourite first-up from a break at Ballarat on September 16, taking off in the last lap before getting tired and breaking. It’s hard to know how he was travelling when he made a mistake, but the form in his prior campaign was good and he’s surely good enough to win a maiden soon. NONREMARKABLE (1) hasn’t shown a great deal at the trials despite winning his last one but gets the services of James Herbertson, while the well-named WHEREDASUNDONTSHINE (3) – who is out of the mare Gluteus Maximus – is maybe next best but the others could all fill the minor end of the prize without surprising. SELECTIONS: SERIOUSLY SAL (2), THE WOOL BROKER (4), NONREMARKABLE (1), WHEREDASUNDONTSHINE (3)

OVERVIEW: ROSBERG (3) was a very good winner for this grade of horse in a race at Melton two starts ago when sitting parked, putting away the leader and then hanging on for victory. He was trapped in the same spot last time out at Ballarat, put away the leader again, but faded late to be beaten 10.7m in what was a solid run. Not sure he gets it any easier here, but I think he’ll be hard to stop regardless of where he ends up in the run. KEAYANG HUSTLER (6) is the obvious, and sometimes the obvious is the best way to go. He’s had two starts for two good wins, and while the times haven’t been off the charts by any means, the trotting-bred son of Bold Eagle is sure to be going close. BRAVE ART (1) has had two runs for smart trainer Carson Millar, with her latest being an encouraging front-running display at Ballarat when only grabbed late. Gate one, sprint trip – tick, tick. LENARD ESS (4) is set to step out for his 200th career start, and he’s the other one with a good chance. BACK: ROSBERG (3) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: ROSBERG (3), KEAYANG HUSTLER (6), BRAVE ART (1), LENARD ESS (4) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R3 #1 ALLWATFUNJINGLES – 1.5 units (each-way) R4 #2 BANIA – 2 units (win) R5 #4 COLTRANE – 3 units (win) R7 #3 ROSBERG – 2 units (win) EARLY QUADDIE 5,6,7,10/9,10/1,2,4,5/2,8 QUADDIE 2,8/4,5,6,7/1,2,4/1,3,4,6 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

The usuals combine again in a small field for the 75 to 105 class runners, where you would expect WATERMELON SUGAR (3) to again press hard for the front in an attempt to cross CUZZY BRO (1), which he did successfully the last time these two met. This should set up a solid tempo from the get-go in what looks a very even field. GO THE RED (2) could be the beneficiary if the other two have a dig at each other early and has loomed as a winning chance a few times of late. MAGICIAN (6) is clearly the class horse of the field at his best and would take plenty of holding out late if anywhere near fit. He has clearly had some issues over the past 12 months and wore quite a bit of gear in a recent trial, which was noticeable, but it wouldn't surprise to see him win this easily. IRON CLAD (4) and COLBY SANZ (5) will also be relying on some good tempo and a consistent pace throughout, although both rise slightly in class here. Selections:GO THE RED (2), MAGICIAN (6),WATERMELON SUGAR (3), CUZZY BRO (1)

The lowest-class race of the night brings together an even field, but happy to side with PUNTARNO STRIDE (9), who has put together some handy performances of late when doing work throughout and not being beaten far. From the nice trailing back-row draw, he should have options as to when to make his move and could be hard to hold out late. ROSE NOIRE (5) hasn't been far away of late and should appreciate the smaller field. Despite the awkward draw, she should be running home strongly. GOT THE GLOW (2) drops back in grade from what she has been competing against recently and gets her chance to return to form from the nice draw, settling on speed. DANCINGWIVJOLENE (1) has been somewhat disappointing in her two runs back from a break but should be nearing peak fitness now and gets her chance from the pole to at least run a place for her connections. LA PIERRE (4) is first up for the new stable and can never be discounted in these sorts of races, while CHRIS BE QUICK (6) and NO NUKES SKIPPER (7) will be relying on some tempo throughout to allow them to run home strongly. Selections:PUNTARNO STRIDE (9), GOT THE GLOW (2), ROSE NOIRE (5), DANCINWIVJOLENE (1)

The maidens once again do battle over the mile, where I suspect we may see ARRIVAL TIME driven aggressively forward from the middle front-row draw in an attempt to find the front. If that does eventuate, he could take some running down. CHASING THE ACE (3) should be much improved from his debut effort, where she battled on okay after doing work in the death seat. LETHAL REPLICA (5) is an improving filly who will no doubt win one soon with the right run in transit, which she will be hoping to get here. SOHO PINA COLADA (6) clearly has ability but rarely puts it all together. If she does pace all the way here, she could take some holding out late. VOODOO RANGER (2) and CRUNCHTHEGUN (9) will no doubt loom as chances again and should get nice runs in transit from their inside draws on the front and back rows respectively. Selections:ARRIVAL TIME (4), CHASING THE ACE (3), LETHAL REPLICA (5), VOODOO RANGER (2)

CHEYS ANGEL (3) put two wins together before having no luck last start when driven for luck from the wide gate. If she is able to cross to the pegs here before possibly handing up to LETSGOBRO (4), who should be driven aggressively and usually does his best racing over the mile, they may be hard to catch over the short distance. SOHO TIGER LILY (8) is a three-year-old filly who has run some handy times over the mile but draws an awkward gate here and will need some luck late. WEONA EAGLE (9) and QUETZALLI (10) are the highest-class horses in the field using the mares claim and will no doubt both be running home strongly if there is any tempo at all throughout the race. Selections:LETSGOBRO (4), CHEYS ANGEL (3), WEONA EAGLE (9), QUETZALLI (10)

Another race over the short-course distance where there are some handy types involved, including MUZZAME MATE (2). He deserves to win a race after some handy performances of late without breaking through. He may have enough gate speed to find the pegs here, can run a very slick mile when required and looks the hardest to beat. PREPARATION (1) looks to have good talent but is still learning his racecraft, and if he is able to kick through and hold a forward position off a handy speed, he could be dangerous late if the gaps come his way. CENTURIAN MISS (4) and ART HUNTSMAN (7) both possess superior gate speed and may look to use that early in an attempt to find the pegs or a forward position, which would give them their best chance. DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (5) is possibly racing in career-best form and has been super consistent of late. If he is able to get a nice run in transit, he could take some holding out late. Selections:MUZZAME MATE (2), DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (5), PREPARATION (1), CENTURIAN MISS (4)

OUR ULTIMATE GRACY (1) looks very well placed here from the pole draw over the mile distance using the double claim. She should have enough gate speed to hold out the other fast beginners in OUR SWEET TRIXIE (4) and JUST LIKE A DREAM (3) and take plenty of running down if she holds the form from her first two starts since arriving in the state for the new camp. LIKEABLE ROGUE (5), IFYOULOVEMELETMEGO (6) and TALK IS CHEAP (7) also possess good gate speed, but suspect they may have to be driven more quietly here, with the three runners to their inside appearing to have enough speed to hold them out early. REPETITIVE (8) and MIKI SANZ (9) should get nice runs from their soft back-row draws and will be hoping the gaps appear late to allow them to run home strongly, as will GOBSMACKED (12), who can never be ruled out in these sorts of races, although it is always difficult to win from barrier 12 over the mile. Selections:OUR ULTIMATE GRACY (1), JUST LIKE A DREAM (3), OUR SWEET TRIXIE (4), GOBSMACKED (12)

Although it looks like an awkward draw for IYLAC CHAMBER (8), I think the polemarker in ASTORMZABREWEN (1) should have sufficient gate speed to kick up and hold the front if they so desire, which would aid the former’s chances if the gaps come his way late. OMYBACNKNEES JUDGE (3) has been good at his past two starts without winning and should again sit on speed and no doubt loom as a chance in the finish. JILLIBY WORPA (4), WINNING BREW (5) and ULTIMATE GLADIATOR (6) have all been putting in strong performances and will look to push forward from their awkward front-row draws to find positions on speed. QUALIFY (9) and SPORTZSILK (10) both returned to their best form when runner-up last start and should get nice runs in transit, bringing them right into the finish if there is some solid tempo throughout. Selections:IYLAC CHAMBER (8), WINNING BREW (5), QUALIFY (9), JILLIBY WORPA (4)

PORT RUN MACHINE (2) was very impressive last start when taking on the older horses, sitting outside the leader and running a very slick last half to win easily, albeit they did get away with a soft first half. There looks to be some good gate speed from numerous front-row runners here, so Gareth will have options from the draw, but he clearly looks the most progressive horse in the field. WEE GEORGIE WOOD (1) will be looking to hold up from the pole draw, where he does his best racing, and should be right in the finish. OUR WILLOW (3) and LAID BACK (4) will also be looking to use their good gate speed to find positions on speed. If the front-row runners overdo it early, there are numerous horses off the back row capable of finishing home strongly, including MERRYWOOD PAUL (11), who is threatening to break through for trainer Brent Norton, and MOVESLIKEALADY (13), who will need another special drive weaving through the pack to win from the draw but can't be discounted. HAY MIKI (6) draws another awkward gate, as he usually does, but at his best could be running home strongly out wide into the finish. Selections:PORT RUN MACHINE (2), WEE GEORGIE WOOD (1), MERRYWOOD PAUL (11), HAY MIKI (6) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:HOOKLINEANDSINKER (2) has improved with every start since returning from a spell and worked forward to find the lead when he scored at Globe Derby last outing. He is drawn to lead again and should take catching over the sprint distance. CALF PEN (6) has returned to his peak form having been placed at his past four attempts. He worked hard when second at Mildura two starts ago then followed with a third against a strong line up at Horsham. ALWAYS ON SAFARI (5) is a fast beginner and has been racing well enough to feature prominently. He held his own after having an economical run at his latest third in South Australia. LOWER MANHATTAN (11) was placed twice in succession prior striking trouble at Globe Derby last outing. He is poorly drawn but should be finding the line well SELECTIONS: HOOKLINEANDSINKER (2), CALF PEN (6), ALWAYS ON SAFARI (5), LOWER MANHATTAN (11)

OVERVIEW:BETTORBUST (10) is a smart juvenile that should strip fitter from his first up fourth at Wagga, where he raced greenly in the early stages and eventually took cover behind the leader. He performed extremely well at the trials prior and he appears to be well suited against this line up. SNEAKY PHILTRA (9) returned to her peak form when she sprinted home best to win over ACCELERE (6) and CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (2) at Mildura last outing. She is awkwardly drawn but should be finding the line strongly again. CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (2) performs best when he is able to lead and finally gains the right draw to obtain a prominent position so he is worth an investment. MY ULTIMATE HENRY (1) delivered a career best performance to win at Mildura last outing and is drawn to receive the perfect trip so he must be respected. BACK: BETTORBUST (10) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: BETTORBUST (10), SNEAKY PHILTRA (9), CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (2), MY ULTIMATE HENRY (1)

OVERVIEW: SHEER ME (3) pushed forward to find the lead and won comfortably at Kilmore then followed with an unplaced run against a strong field at Wagga. She should give a bold showing from her good draw at her Mildura debut. HILLTOP CRUNCH (5) followed a fourth in the SA Australian Gold Final in June with a win in the Sales Classic at Port Pirie. He is widely drawn but is a promising juvenile and should run a good race again. SURETHING (4) is resuming since a Mildura victory back in June and hasn’t been to the trials. She is a nicely bred filly and has the ability to figure in the finish. LIKE A LIBRARIAN (1) will appreciate her best draw for a long time and is a possible improver. SELECTIONS: SHEER ME (3), HILLTOP CRUNCH (5), SURETHING (4), LIKE A LIBRARIAN (1)

OVERVIEW: MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (6) began quickly and pushed forward to find the lead when he won comfortably at his first run since June. All of his ten career victories have been at Mildura and he is the class runner of the field so he can overcome the poor draw. LETSGO BIG GIRL (2) performs best when she is able to lead over the sprint distance so she has the conditions to suit her here. She finished off solidly from the second half of the field when a close third at her latest Mildura performance. DALLAS MIKI (5) is resuming since a third at Mildura in July but he led throughout at a recent trial success. He is very strong and likes to roll along at a genuine tempo so he is sure to make his presence felt. PRIORITISE (8) endured a tough run when a creditable fourth behind Wipeout at Mildura after a second behind My Ultimate Jimmy. He is worth thought along with DEMON BLUE (7), which is making his local debut. SELECTIONS: MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (6), LETSGO BIG GIRL (2), DALLAS MIKI (5), PRIORITISE (8)

OVERVIEW:THE GOLDEN HOOK (7) is racing in outstanding form and looms as the horse to beat again despite the awkward draw. He won by nearly 30m at Gawler, fought very hard when second in the Mildura Guineas then scored comfortably at Mildura last outing. LISTEN TO THE HAND (3) led throughout in two victories at Mildura and Gawler prior to an unplaced effort in the Mildura Guineas. He disappointed last time out but is capable of better and should give a forward showing. FOXY TWO GLOVES (4) is resuming since a sixth behind Dallas Miki in March. She was racing against much tougher opposition when she was last in work so she is capable of featuring prominently if she is somewhere near her peak. MIDNIGHT PIRATE (5) led out then took cover when second behind THE GOLDEN HOOK (7) last outing. He might not be able to get across to the markers from his awkward draw here but he is racing well enough to be competitive. BACK: THE GOLDEN HOOK (7) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: THE GOLDEN HOOK (7), LISTEN TO THE HAND (3), FOXY TWO GLOVES (4), MIDNIGHT PIRATE (5)

OVERVIEW:YARRAMAN JOLT (3) is a speedy pacer, which has performed well in two Mildura attempts, which has yielded a win and a third. He is ideally drawn for this assignment and should give a bold showing. MY ULTIMATE BILLY (7) hasn’t won a race since March 2024 but he is better than that statistic suggests and appears to be well graded in this event so he is not without a chance. ROYAL SAXON (8) scored after trailing the leader two starts ago then was caught behind tiring runners at his latest sixth. He prefers to race close to the pace so being drawn on the second line is a disadvantage but he is likely to be strongly fancied. SHES POPPY (4) is rising in class on her latest good performances but she is fast beginner and is drawn to be prominent throughout. SELECTIONS: YARRAMAN JOLT (3), MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (7), ROYAL SAXON (8), SHES POPPY (4)

OVERVIEW: THE END (7) is a nicely bred colt, which has shown a lot of ability at the trials and strikes a very suitable assignment first up. He won at his latest trial appearance over the smart filly Sabalenka at Shepparton. LATHER WITH FIRE (4) wasn’t beaten by far at her first two Mildura appearances prior to her latest two efforts in the South-East. She appears to be better suited under these conditions and is worth thought. MISS CULLEN (3) ran a better race after trailing the leader at Mildura last outing and is a good chance of finding the same position from her good draw so she must be considered as a place chance again. FEARLESS SNIPER (5) should have benefited from her first up performance at Swan Hill, where he finished eighth but didn’t perform badly and is not without a chance. SANTA CASA LEVI (6) is resuming from a spell and hasn’t been to the trials but she is a speedy type and is worth thought in multiple combinations. BACK: THE END (7) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: THE END (7), LATHER WITH FIRE (4), MISS CULLEN (3), FEARLESS SNIPER (5)

OVERVIEW: EAGLEYE (7) settled midfield and made ground out wide on the track when third behind Bettor Doo at Shepparton last outing. She was placed behind Soho Amaryllis in a much stronger race at Melton on September 18 so she appears to be hard to beat against this line up. FLEUR BELLA (3) raced without cover throughout, pulled hard and produced a big performance to win at Mildura last outing. She was impressive last time and will take plenty of catching if she is able to find the lead. SUNSHINE WARRIOR (5) led throughout to score at Mildura on September 27. He was safely held behind FLEUR BELLA (3) at his latest attempt but he is worth another chance. BIG BAD CHAD (2) is resuming since July but he was able to win a trial at Mildura recently and performs best when he is close to the speed so he cannot be discarded. SELECTIONS: EAGLEYE (7), FLEUR BELLA (3), SUNSHINE WARRIOR (5), BIG BAD CHAD (2)

OVERVIEW: KEAYANG CRIPPA (6) has been promising a win for some time and will be aided by the small field of seven runners so he must be considered as one of the leading chances. He attempted to lead throughout when second behind the South Australian pacer Keilah two starts ago then got a long way back from a similar bad draw at his latest appearance. HESASTAR (7) was able to lead throughout at Mildura three starts ago and this race is of similar standard. He is likely to make a move once the pace slackens during the middle stages and is worth an investment. BOHEMIAN BRAIDS (5) is a fast beginner and will appreciate a drop back in class for this assignment. He was runner up at Swan Hill on Thursday after leading out then taking cover and should give a forward showing under these conditions. DIAMOND KRUSHER (4) led throughout at a Mildura victory four starts ago and is not without a chance from her reasonable draw. SELECTIONS: KEAYANG CRIPPA (6), HESASTAR (7), BOHEMIAN BRAIDS (5), DIAMOND KRUSHER (4)

OVERVIEW: PHILS BOY (3) was left stranded without cover and battled on well for third behind Feefifofum at Mildura last outing, beating most of tonight’s rivals in the process. He appears to be well placed against this line up and gets his chance to break through for a win. LITLMAX (1) is a first starter for trainer Brendan Tune, which scored in slow time at a recent Mildura trial effort. He is ideally drawn first up and should receive every chance. CHEDDAR CHEESE (2) was resuming since July and making his Mildura debut when fourth to Edgar Bromac last outing. He should have benefited from that performance and should give a forward showing. CRUEL MISTRESS (7) was placed from behind the leader at Mildura on August 21 and has the perfect trailing draw so she is a minor place chance again. She did run a reasonable race when fourth at Swan Hill on Thursday. BACK: PHILS BOY (3) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: PHILS BOY (3), LITLMAX (1), CHEDDAR CHEESE (2), CRUEL MISTRESS (7)

OVERVIEW: One of the great meetings of the year is upon us, and Victoria Cup night kicks off with a clash for horses who have not won any race with advertised stakemoney of $15,000 or more. NEATNTIDY (4) gets a great chance with the services of master reinsman Luke McCarthy, who takes charge of the Aaron Dunn-trained pacer third-up in the campaign. He was a soft winner at Mildura first-up and last Friday had a little look for the front, drifted back along the pegs and then had no clear air in the home straight while only being beaten 2.8m by Earl Of Pembroke. I fancy he’s a chance of finding the top, and from there would get his chance. HITCH TO HIS STAR (6) was a winner at Melton in early September and has run creditable races in good company since, VIVID DREAM (5) won his first two starts for new trainer Dean Braun in Tasmania and was very competitive when sixth in a Victoria Derby heat last weekend, while ALL BLAZING GUNS (10) has been closing off nicely in recent runs and is one at odds worth considering along with WOTDIDUSAAAY (3), who has won his past two. BACK: NEATNTIDY (4) – 1 unit (each-way) SELECTIONS: NEATNTIDY (4), HITCH TO HIS STAR (6), VIVID DREAM (5), ALL BLAZING GUNS (10)

OVERVIEW: The first of five Group 1s is the Victoria Trotters Oaks where HALLEBESOFINE (4) gets another good shot at a maiden elite-level triumph for trainer-driver Tina Ridis. Seven of these horses contested last weekend’s G1 Need For Speed Princess Final won by HARPERSEVEN (8), but HALLEBESOFINE (4) had no luck there as favourite when caught wide from a bad gate over the sprint trip. She was only beaten 11.6m, and before that beat home five rivals that reoppose in the G1 Vicbred Super Series Final when second to Queen Of Sees from the front. I fancy she might be able to wrestle the top off quick beginner JILLIBY RADIANCE (3), and if that’s the case, I’m happily in her corner. ALDEBARAN ADA (1) was caught parked and did a great job to run second in the Princess last weekend, now draws beautifully in gate one, ADELAIDE RED (9) endured a similar run against older horses at Ballarat last week and didn’t beat one home, but was probably the best run in that Vicbred showdown when coming off speed for third, while HARPERSEVEN (8) is now a two-time Group 1 winner and has obvious claims. This field doesn’t appear to have any standout filly and the horse with the best run might just prevail! BACK: HALLEBESOFINE (4) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: HALLEBESOFINE (4), ALDEBARAN ADA (1), ADELAIDE RED (9), HARPERSEVEN (8)

OVERVIEW: THE ART OF SUCCESS (11) is shooting for an amazing 11th successive win in this Group 3 Ladyship Cup, and while I’m not exactly sure how she achieves it, I’m not willing to go against her. Last time out, she sat parked to WICKED CONFESSION (7) in the Vicbred Super Series Final for four-year-old mares and wore her down late to score a brilliant victory. That was over 2240m and this is back to 1720m which makes things much harder, but she’s just such an impressive horse coming through the ranks. I’m probably not willing to bet at $2, but can’t tip against her. SWEET IDEAL (2) is flying for Team Lawlor with wins in her past three and draws to find the pegs so will be hard to hold out, LET HER ROLL (4) ran fourth in that Vicbred final behind THE ART OF SUCCESS (11) but had a horror draw and flat tyre, while WICKED CONFESSION (7) is also very good and would be a chance if she was able to spear across to lead over the sprint trip. Great race! SELECTIONS: THE ART OF SUCCESS (11), SWEET IDEAL (2), LET HER ROLL (4), WICKED CONFESSION (7)

OVERVIEW: Great edition of the Victoria Derby where the early speed battle will likely prove telling, with three of the big guns in the market drawn on the front row. They’re favourite PALLADIUM (4), fellow NSW pacer NYMBAL (3) and BROOKLYN DAN (1). All three clashed in the Queensland Derby back in July, with NYMBAL (3) able to cross BROOKLYN DAN (1) at the start from similar gates before PALLADIUM (4) sat parked to score in a close finish. Since then, the winner’s trainer-driver Brad Hewitt has declared this in an interview with Adam Hamilton: “As good as he was that night, I’m sure he’s a lot better now. He had a really rushed and interrupted preparation for Queensland, but since the break he had after it, he’s come back a different horse”. If NYMBAL (3) crosses early, I sense he will hand to PALLADIUM (4) like he did in the heat last weekend, and from there the latter would be the one to beat. NYMBAL (3) beat PALLADIUM (4) in a recent clash at Menangle despite having no luck and could have claimed that Queensland Derby with clearer air late, ENJOY LIFE (9) has only ever been beaten once and was a very impressive winner coming off speed in his Derby heat last Saturday, while BROOKLYN DAN (1) also won a qualifier last weekend and has obvious claims from the good gate. Others in contention are Mick Stanley pair SOHO TRUMP (11) and SOHO CHARMER (12), MOUNT BARKER BOY (13) and LE CARDINAL (2). SELECTIONS: PALLADIUM (4), ENJOY LIFE (9), NYMBAL (3), BROOKLYN DAN (1)

OVERVIEW: Wide-open Group 1 Bill Collins Trotters Sprint where preference is with I AM WILMA (1) who draws wonderfully in gate one and heads into this assignment on the back of a lovely trial where she beat two pacers and GOTFEELINGSYOUKNOW (5) at Melton on October 6. Her last run was a very brave runner-up placing behind GATESYS GEM (2) in the Group 1 Vicbred Super Series Final for four-year-old trotting mares when she had a back row draw and sat parked for most of the race. She has gate speed and a great chance from the pole over the 1720m. LOVEMETO (6) struggled from a similar draw over this trip first-up but bounced back in a big way over 2240m last weekend winning the Dullard Cup against four rivals that reoppose, ROCKINWITHATTITUDE (9) is a multiple Group 1 winner who couldn’t overcome her big handicap in the McNamara Memorial Trotters Cup at Geelong latest when beaten by a front-running IMPERIAL MONARCH (4) but is without doubt one of the top squaregaiters in the land, while Italian GANDHI MAIL (7) brings down good NSW form from five starts there and might be the speed horse from wide on the front line. Great race and the chances don’t stop with those mentioned. BACK: I AM WILMA (1) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: I AM WILMA (1), LOVEMETO (6), ROCKINWITHATTITUDE (9), GANDHI MAIL (7)

OVERVIEW: The big one is the $250,000 SEN Victoria Cup at Group 1 level and it looks set to be dominated by wonder mare CAPTAINS MISTRESS (3) after she landed a very favourable gate at Tuesday’s barrier draw. She is the reigning Inter Dominion champion after beating all-time great Leap To Fame in a memorable final in July and returned from a freshen with a front-running success at Menangle on October 3. It’s hard to see a world where she doesn’t lead and win to give Jason Grimson and Cameron Hart a second victory in the race after taking it with Swayzee in 2024. KINGMAN (8) is the defending Victoria Cup champion, ran a great race for second behind CAPTAINS MISTRESS (3) on October 3 and would have been a genuine threat from a better gate, CATCH A WAVE (9) is the winningest Group 1 starter in the field with eight and can be lethal late from two on the second row, while FIGHTER COMMAND (6), fast beginner NYACK (5), the well-drawn SMOKEN ACE (2) and last weekend’s Smoken Up Sprint winner BULLETPROOF BOY (4) are among the rest of the chances who are all probably running for second and third. BACK: KINGMAN (8) – 2 units (place) SELECTIONS: CAPTAINS MISTRESS (3), KINGMAN (8), CATCH A WAVE (9), FIGHTER COMMAND (6)

OVERVIEW: BETTOR BEACH (4) is the short-priced favourite for the Group 1 Victoria Oaks and deservedly so. She won the G1 Vicbred Super Series Final for three-year-old fillies in effortless fashion back on September 13 and dominated her Oaks heat last weekend despite being put to pressure by THE QUEENS GAMBIT (7) with a sizzling 25.6 third quarter which she seemed to handle easily. She’s the one that has to go on top. There could be some fireworks early with RIPPLES (6) – who was able to cross WILLOWS GIRL (2) from similar draws before being run down by that rival in the other qualifier – likely to launch again. I’m not sure Mark Pitt did everything he could to hold RIPPLES (6) there, so perhaps WILLOWS GIRL (2) can dig up to hold out the early challenge with BETTOR BEACH (4) then likely to find the top. THE QUEENS GAMBIT (7) ran well in the heat from a back row draw and it’ll be interesting to see what she does now drawn on the front line, while RIPPLES (6) and SWEET IRISH LOCH (3) are the other leading hopes. SELECTIONS: BETTOR BEACH (4), WILLOWS GIRL (2), THE QUEENS GAMBIT (7), RIPPLES (6)

OVERVIEW: OUR SUNSET DELIGHT (5) is emergency for the SEN Victoria Cup and gains a start here if there’s no scratchings from the night’s big feature. He looks very well placed, particularly if he’s able to work forward and assume control. Last weekend in the Smoken Up Sprint, he led, handed to Fighter Command, went straight past him in the straight and just missed Bulletproof Boy who had all the momentum. That followed two dominant wins at Menangle. CIGANO (6) was breathtaking coming from off speed with a personal last half of 53.25 while running down Wicked Confession to score brilliantly at Melton on October 2. He’s very fast and might be too slick with the right trip. COASTAL DRIVE (2) sat parked and won a much easier race than this at Geelong a fortnight ago and has claims if he’s able to find the fence, while multiple free-for-all winner YAMBUKIAN (9) is first-up in more than a year but trialled nicely at Melton for his return and oozes class. GHOST OF TIME (4), HESITATE (7) and TRIPLE EIGHT (8) are others that could win without surprising. SELECTIONS: OUR SUNSET DELIGHT (5), CIGANO (6), COASTAL DRIVE (2), YAMBUKIAN (9)

OVERVIEW: JACCKA EVAN (7) has been very impressive since arriving from New Zealand, winning his first two starts at Wagga and Kilmore before an unlucky third at Melton last time out. His win sitting parked to the handy Atua Magic two back was very tough, and he looked ready to sprint past rivals but couldn’t get clear late when third to Royal Appointment. Reckon he’s pretty handy, so happy his way. SCHWARZ (8) was second-up back in the care of Emma Stewart when he worked forward from the back row, found the top and held on for victory at Geelong a fortnight ago. It was a good win without being amazing, and he’s a nice, progressive type from a powerful yard so must be respected. MY LITTLE BO (3) is first-up following a break and trialled really nicely at Melton for her return, while ISOLATION (6) was plain last time out behind winner OLLIES THE BOSS (5) at Geelong, but is worth another chance based on his form from earlier in the campaign. Not much would surprise here! BACK: JACCKA EVAN (7) – 1 unit (each-way) SELECTIONS: JACCKA EVAN (7), SCHWARZ (8), MY LITTLE BO (3), ISOLATION (6) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R1 #4 NEATNTIDY – 1 unit (each-way) R2 #4 HALLEBESOFINE – 2 units (win) R5 #1 I AM WILMA – 2 units (win) R6 #8 KINGMAN – 2 units (place) R9 #7 JACCKA EVAN – 1 unit (each-way) EARLY QUADDIE 4,5,6,10/1,4,8,9/2,4,7,11/1,3,4,9 QUADDIE 1,6,7,9/3/4/5,6 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:JILLIBY ZUCCHINI (7) settled at the rear of the field, came out three horses wide from the 1200m and moved up on the outside of the leader from the 900m when a big winner at Horsham in a slick mile rate of 1.55.5 last outing. She moves to the front line now and should prove hard to beat again. BLACK OPAL JACK (11) is resuming since a second at Horsham in June but he won a trial over Wicked Hangover on October 05. He is a smart type and should make his presence felt. The Matthew Craven trained pair JOE GOT ROLLED (2) and LOU EASYANA (6) are both resuming and haven’t been to the trials but they were competing against stronger opposition when they were last in work so they are worth thought. YNOBE NOVA (3) and HUXHAM CHUBB (4) are both racing well enough to figure in the finish. SELECTIONS: JILLIBY ZUCCHINI (7), BLACK OPAL JACK (11), JOE GOT ROLLED (2), LOU EASYANA (6)

OVERVIEW:DISPERSION (1) trailed the leader, used the sprint lane and just failed to pick up Lambro Louella in a slick last quarter of 27.9 seconds at Horsham. He has shown a lot of ability at his three placed efforts to date and he should be winning a race in the near future. COLOSIMO (4) is a handy 3yo pacer, which performed well at the trials prior to his game first up third in a sizzling mile rate of 1.54.9 at Ballarat on Thursday night. He is very versatile and looms as one of the leading chances. BRIDWOOD MAISEY (8) is awkwardly drawn but she is a classy filly and should go well. She was resuming since an unplaced effort in the Breeders Crown Final when a handy third behind Keayang Hustler at Horsham. LOUS MAMBO (2) was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished well for fourth behind Regal Rock last time out. He is worth thought along with KEAYANG MARICRUZ (6), which won comfortably against the easier Maiden class at her latest attempt. BACK: DISPERSION (1) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: DISPERSION (1), COLOSIMO (4), BRIDWOOD MAISEY (8), LOUS MAMBO (2)

OVERVIEW: SWIM SUIT (1) delivered a career best performance when he produced a big finale out wide on the track and finished a close up third in a slick mile rate of 1.56.7 at Maryborough on Monday. He is ideally drawn and gets his chance to break through for a win. BANGBANG BOBBIE (9) enjoyed a soft trip and hit the line strongly for second behind Captain Hank at Melton last outing. This race is no harder and he should be running home well again. LITTLEBYLITTLE (3) is a first starter for trainer Nicholas O’Connor, which has been performing well at the trials. He is worth thought from his good draw. KEAYANG ALABAMA (7) should be fitter after his first up fifth at Kilmore and JILLIBY UTAH (8) didn’t have much luck in the straight at Ballarat on Thursday night and is a place chance from his trailing draw. BACK: SWIM SUIT (1) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: SWIM SUIT (1), BANGBANG BOBBIE (9), LITTLEBYLITTLE (3), KEAYANG ALABAMA (7)

OVERVIEW: HAPPILY (1) will appreciate a big drop back in class on her latest eighth in the Super Series Final behind the star mare Theartofsuccess and will prove very hard to beat. She finished third in a heat of that series and was a very unlucky second at Ballarat three starts ago. JILLIBY SNIPER (2) is the obvious danger. He won twice in succession prior to contesting a heat of the Victoria Derby series. He boasts the strong record of four wins from just eight starts. RANGER RICK (5) has been placed in 12 of his 16 starts for the season without winning. He ran his usual honest race when a close third behind El Boston at Maryborough on Monday and is worth a ticket each way. BROWNIESATMIDNIGHT (8) is a speedy type that will have benefited from his first up run and is worth thought from his trailing draw. BACK: HAPPILY (1) – 1.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: HAPPILY (1), JILLIBY SNIPER (2), RANGER RICK (5), BROWNIESATMIDNIGHT (8)

OVERVIEW:DOCTOR GO JOH (8) is racing in good form against similar opposition and is a winning chance again. He was able to find the front at his two recent victories and he has drawn on the second line now but he is meeting very similar opposition here. HAVADASH JOH (4) will appreciate a drop back in class on his latest performances and is capable of improving on his numerical form. He loomed up to win but cost himself victory by breaking stride in the latter stages at Charlton last time out. SMOKIN STREPO (6) was resuming since a Mount Gambier victory in June when a creditable second behind THE IRISHMAN (7) on Tuesday night. He should have benefited from that run and is capable of going one better. THE IRISHMAN (7) was driven aggressively to find the lead in the early stages and held on to win at Mount Gambier. He has been racing well against this class and is worth thought again. SELECTIONS: DOCTOR GO JOH (8), HAVADASH JOH (4), SMOKIN STREPO (6), THE IRISHMAN (7)

OVERVIEW:KEAYANG MINNESOTA (8) has galloped at her only two standing start performances to date but she will take beating if she delivers a fool proof display. She circled around to park without cover and won untouched when an impressive winner at Kilmore on Wednesday night. JAKARTA (7) was a winner under similar conditions at Terang on August 30. He sprinted quickly from midfield to join the leaders in the home straight and just peaked on his run over the final stages when a close up third behind Why Now at Ballarat last outing. HAPPY ESCAPE (6) began quickly from the standing start, raced without cover throughout and battled on too well to score at Mount Gambier last outing. This is a race of more depth but he is worth thought again. SNICKERS EXPRESS (5) has been racing consistently against similar opposition and is worth a ticket each way. SELECTIONS: KEAYANG MINNESOTA (8), JAKARTA (7), HAPPY ESCAPE (6), SNICKERS EXPRESS (5)

OVERVIEW: KEAYANG GYPSY (4) settled midfield, came out three horses wide from the 600m and finished a close third at Geelong prior to working hard and peaking late in a strong race at Melton. She is proven from the standing start and should take beating under these conditions. OFF YOUR FACESKI (3) commenced from the handicap of 30m and raced without cover for the last lap when a strong winner at Terang two starts ago then followed with a big win in the Swan Hill Trotters Cup. He is likely to push forward to find a handy position shortly after the start and should go well again. BOUTIKA (2) is racing in career best form having won three races in succession including a track record breaking performance at Ararat, followed by a third at Maryborough on Monday. She continues to step up in grade but she must be included amongst the leading chances. KEAYANG LAVITA (5) commenced from the massive handicap of 60m when third behind OFF YOUR FACESKI (3) at Terang two starts ago. The handicap of 40m is still a big test but she warrants consideration. SELECTIONS: KEAYANG GYPSY (4), OFF YOUR FACESKI (3), BOUTIKA (2), KEAYANG LAVITA (5)

OVERVIEW: RAPTA (3) has been competing at a high level and is likely to find this assignment to be much easier. He finished fifth in Super Series Final, followed with a win at Charlton then competed in the Need For Speed Prince series, where second in a heat and unplaced in the Final. MISS MUSCLE (5) is backing up quickly from her effort at Geelong on Friday night but she is a talented juvenile trotter, which should run her usual honest race. She finished fourth in the juvenile section of the Super Series three starts ago and tried hard when a close second behind Night Flight at her next attempt. TAURAS (6) has performed well in both of his efforts since resuming and was a runaway winner in a Maiden event at Horsham last outing. This is a race of more depth but he cannot be left out of calculations. ARGYLE MUSE (4) was doing her best work at the end when a handy third behind The Chook last outing. She is yet to win in 14 starts but must be considered as a place chance again. BACK: RAPTA (3) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: RAPTA (3), MISS MUSCLE (5), TAURAS (6), ARGYLE MUSE (4)
